Weekly Family Update - 18.09.26 
Tip: to quickly navigating this online Update, try using the icon on the bottom right of your 
page that will turn this into a quick-access contents page. 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
What makes Abbey College special is what happens beyond the classroom. Our Offer and 
Opportunity Programme (OOPs) gives every student the chance to discover new interests, 
develop talents, make friends and build skills for life. 
This year, we're expanding our offer to more than 50 clubs, teams and activities. From sport, 
music and performance to technology, creativity and academic enrichment, there is 
something for everyone. 
We expect every student to take part in at least one extra-curricular activity. 
Information on how to sign up through MCAS will be shared in the coming weeks. More clubs 
are still being added as staff finalise plans, including some exciting and unexpected 
opportunities. 
We have an exciting year ahead and look forward to seeing students make the most of 
everything on offer. Thank you, as always, for your continued support. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 
 

Please read on for essential updates.

Click here: https://www.abbey.college/vacancies

Headteacher Commendations w/c 14/09/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 
 
Staff member of the week 
Ms Cornthwaite –   Intuition: Well done for settling in so well to your role in the SSO team. 
Your friendly face and presence are much needed for our students! 

Tell us about something brilliant! 
If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college .

Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Up to date details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 
You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Diary Dates  
 

Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 
Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Online Safety 
This week students discussed online safety, including personal information, privacy settings, 
online relationships and reporting concerns. 
We reminded students that not everyone online is who they claim to be and encouraged 
them to speak to a trusted adult if any online interaction makes them uncomfortable. 
Useful Resources 
• Internet Matters: https://www.internetmatters.org 
• Childnet: https://www.childnet.com/parents-and-carers 
• UK Safer Internet Centre: https://saferinternet.org.uk 
• CEOP: https://www.ceopeducation.co.uk/parents 

If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college. We are here to help. 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 1 – Life Chances  
Your attendance today shapes your future.  
Every lesson you attend builds skills, confidence, and opportunities for later life—whether 
that’s college, apprenticeships, or careers.  
Turn up, stay focused, and keep your options open.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer

Weekly Family Update - 11.09.26 
Tip: to quickly navigate this online Update, try using the icon on the bottom right of your 
page that will turn this into a quick-access contents page. 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
A very warm welcome back to Abbey College. 
As part of our school community, you play an important role in helping our young people 
succeed. This weekly bulletin helps us stay connected as we work together to support more 
than 1,100 families. 
I would like to begin by congratulating our Year 11 and Year 13 students on their excellent 
examination results. We are incredibly proud of what they have achieved. Three quarters of 
our Year 13 students have secured places at university, 22% have moved into 
apprenticeships, and others have taken exciting steps into employment. Their success reflects 
their hard work, determination, and resilience. 
I would also like to thank our dedicated staff. They give so much of their time and energy to 
support our young people, often going above and beyond to help them achieve their best. 
Today’s Weekly Update shares useful updates for parents and carers about the academic 
year ahead. Please take this opportunity to mark your diaries and explore the signposts to 
support on our website. 
It’s great to get a new school year underway. Come with us! You are welcome! 
Stay Informed: 
• Key dates: Check the school calendar here. 
• Tuesday 29th September 1pm finish: We are hosting our annual open evening for 
prospective Year 6 students on Tuesday 29th September.  In order for us to prepare 
the site for this event, students will be dismissed at 1pm and the buses will depart 
shortly afterwards. 

• Coats: As our building works continue, indoor space for students at break and 
lunchtime is currently limited. To help ensure your child remains comfortable 
throughout the school day, we ask that they bring a suitable coat to school whenever 
wet weather is forecast. 
Communication with School: 
• First Contact: Reach out to your child's tutor first for any queries. 
• Email is preferred for contact. Please only call the main Reception number in an 
emergency or if a situation cannot wait, for example, change of travel plans for your 
child. 
• Staff are expected to respond in a timely manner (see Communications Flowchart at 
the bottom of this Update). Should you email a member of staff and not receive a 
response within the timeframe specified (except for part-time colleagues), please use 
the Parent Forum Guarantee, and I will follow this up.  
Parent Forum Guarantee: 
The Parent Forum Guarantee gives all parents the right to speak directly to the Headteacher 
or Deputy Headteacher, within 24 hours, if you feel your question has not been answered by 
those you have already contacted.  
• Call: 01487 812352 and quote the Parent Forum Guarantee. 
• Email: office@abbey.college using the subject header 'Parent Forum Guarantee.' 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

metadata.title: ‘Popular pub’ to be turned into shop after appeal granted
metadata.contentSnippet: Plans to turn The Bulls Head pub in St Neots into a corner shop have been approved on appeal after an inspector found its loss was “sufficiently justified”.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: ‘Popular pub’ to be turned into shop after appeal granted
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans to turn a pub into a corner shop have been approved on appeal after an inspector found its loss was “sufficiently justified”. The Bulls Head in St Neots shut in August 2023 before being put on market by brewery Greene King as they failed to find a new landlord. Huntingdonshire District Council refused plans from Noble Trading (UK) Ltd to re-open the Cambridge Street building as a “modern convenience store”. The Campaign for Pubs organisation objected as they said it had been a “popular pub which was well supported until its closure”. A licence application for the proposed shop was granted to allow them to sell alcohol, but planning permission was needed for the conversion to go ahead. The council rejected this as it would result in the loss of a pub and community space and they said there wasn’t enough evidence it had been marketed for continued use as a pub. Inspector David Reed of the Planning Inspectorate said the property was marketed over 15 months with a total of 38 enquiries, 16 viewings and one offer “which was withdrawn after a serious water damage incident occurred”. He said that feedback from the viewings “was poor” with potential buyers saying the kitchen was too small, there was no parking and the building was in “poor condition” with “too much work needed”. After the price was reduced it was bought by the current applicant, Mr Jeyaseelan Thambirajah. Mr Reed said that although there are no other pubs in the surrounding area, there are nine within one kilometre. He said: “These include Ye Old Sun, the Ale Taster, The Hyde Park and The Coach House. “This competition was also a likely contributing factor to the lack of interest in a public house use.” The council had said there was no proof certain websites listed in the marketing report were actually used but the inspector said this was “an unwarranted allegation”. They also said the premises were only actively marketed for eleven months and that “the asking price was unrealistic”. Mr Reed said that a gap while an offer proceeds “is standard practice” and the price was within the range of other “local comparable public houses”. He said: “It can be concluded that reasonable steps were taken to market the public house without success”. Permission was granted for the shop to open between 6.30am and 11pm from Monday to Saturday and 8am to 9pm on Sundays and Bank Holidays.

The GCE Hire Fleet United Counties League South fixture was played at Histon. Harvey Henderson, Connor Furlong, Danny Baulk, James Stainsby and Connor Barnes were on target for the visitors. Henderson opened the scoring after four minutes, heading home at the far post from Lewis Burgess’s long throw. The forward movement and delivery gave the away side an early advantage, while Histon goalkeeper Tyler Key was left with little chance. Key then kept out Barnes, who was playing against his former club, after the striker had escaped the home defence. Histon were forced into an early change when Ryan Sharman suffered an injury, with Jake Coxall replacing him after 24 minutes. The hosts briefly threatened through Dan Brown, whose breakaway effort was blocked, but the visitors remained in control. St Neots doubled their lead after 31 minutes when Histon failed to clear a ball across the face of goal, allowing Furlong to finish. The home side missed an opportunity to reduce the deficit when Magloire Muyembe fired over, while Lil Francisco shot wide before half-time. Baulk added a third eight minutes after the interval, meeting a cross from Furlong with a powerful volley which gave Key no opportunity. Histon responded with attacking substitutions, but the changes failed to alter the pattern of the match. St Neots continued to defend comfortably, with their back line breaking up most attempts before they could develop into clear chances. Barnes struck the post with a header, and Histon’s problems deepened when Jonny Hall was sent off after 68 minutes. Stainsby made an immediate impact, scoring one minute after his introduction by chasing down the ball and finishing from a narrow angle. The away side continued to press despite making further substitutions, and Barnes completed the scoring five minutes from time after being set up by Joe Sutton. The result leaves Histon with nine defeats from ten matches, with their only victory coming against Brightlingsea in the FA Cup extra preliminary round.

metadata.title: Jail for uninsured driver who fled Cambs crash scene after killing pedestrian
metadata.contentSnippet: A uninsured driver from Cambridgeshire who fled the scene after hitting and killing a pedestrian has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Jail for uninsured driver who fled Cambs crash scene after killing pedestrian
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A uninsured driver from Cambridgeshire who fled the scene after hitting and killing a pedestrian has been jailed. Marcin Pilarski, 36, struck Sam Pope, 28, as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road, Ramsey Mereside, at just before 11pm on May 11, 2024. The crash was only reported when another driver called 999 after seeing Mr Pope, of Lincoln Road, Peterborough, laying in the road. Emergency services attended but despite their efforts, Mr Pope was declared dead at the scene. In a tribute, his family said: "Sam was a free spirit, who liked to live his life at 100mph and believed that rules were meant to be broken. "We shall miss his smile and crazy sense of humour that would always make you laugh, despite what mood you were in that day. "Sam was a rough diamond with a heart made of gold and will leave a big hole in our lives." Sam Pope was struck as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Less than an hour after the collision, at 11.40pm, police were called by Pilarski’s partner who told them he had returned home in her Vauxhall Astra. She revealed the car was badly damaged, with a smashed windscreen and headlamp, and that there was also blood on the front of the vehicle. The woman said that they lived 15 minutes, about nine and a half miles, from the scene of the fatal crash. Police visited the house where they also noticed the damage to the car, and Pilarski, of Sorrell Avenue, Whittlesey, was arrested in relation to the fatal collision. In a statement, Pilarski’s partner said he had called her at 11pm to tell her he had “hit or killed somebody” who had been in the road, but she had to end the call due to him screaming. She said when he returned home in her damaged car she told him they needed to call the police and he answered, “I know”. In police interview Pilarski answered no comment to most questions. However, he later pleaded guilty to causing death by driving a car without a licence or insurance. He was sentenced at Cambridge Crown Court on Thursday (September 17). He was handed one year and three months in prison. He was also disqualified from driving for four years and six months. The car was badly damaged, with a smashed windscreen and headlamp, and had blood on the front (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) In a victim impact statement, Mr Pope’s family said they had been left feeling angry that Pilarski didn’t seem remorseful and hadn’t apologised for his actions. The statement added: “We hope the memory of the night keeps him up at night like it does us. I don’t really know how as a family we will ever come to terms with this.” Detective Inspector Craig Wheeler, who investigated, said: “Pilarski made a conscious decision to drive his partner’s car without a licence or insurance. “He should never have put himself behind the wheel of a car and my thoughts and sympathies remain with the family and friends of Mr Pope, who needlessly lost his life at such a young age. “No sentence will ever ease the pain of their loss, but I hope the case acts as a stark reminder against getting behind the wheel while uninsured or without a licence. Just one journey could end in tragedy.” Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire girl, 16, suffered fatal head injury in river crash, inquest hears
metadata.contentSnippet: A 16-year-old girl died from a head injury after the car she was travelling in crashed into a river, an inquest heard today.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire girl, 16, suffered fatal head injury in river crash, inquest hears
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A 16-year-old Cambridgeshire girl died from a head injury after the car she was travelling in crashed into a river, an inquest heard today. Four members of Eden Bunn’s family attended the inquest into the horse-loving teenager’s death at Vantage House, Huntingdon. The inquest heard Eden, from Sutton Bridge, was sitting in the middle of the rear seat of a Volkswagen Polo driven by Declan Berry when it ended up in the River Nene at Wisbech on March 17. Eden Bunn loved her horses. (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Ms Gray heard evidence from a collision report prepared by police accident investigators. The report said Mr Berry, 18, was driving the Polo at about 90mph on North Brink, Wisbech, at around 8.19pm when it hit a pothole, left the road, rolled several times and plunged into the fast-flowing river. Three other teenagers, all aged 18, were in the car with Eden and Mr Berry. Mr Berry also died, and his body was recovered from the river at Wisbech Marian nearly two weeks later. The many floral tributes that were left by the River Nene in Wisbech after the fatal crash that claimed the life of Eden Bunn. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Three of the passengers escaped the submerged car, but Eden did not get out. Her body was recovered the following day. A post-mortem found that Eden’s severe head injury was the primary cause of death. Ms Gray said there was no evidence of water in her lungs. The collision report blamed the car’s speed but said the road’s potholes, crumbling edges, undulating, and uneven surface also played a “less than minimal” part in the crash. Declan Berry had been driving the VW Polo in which Eden was a passenger. (Image: Cambridgeshire Constabulary) The three surviving passengers said Mr Berry was driving fast and that the front-seat passenger told him to slow down moments before the crash after noting he was doing 90mph. A female rear-seat passenger said Eden also shouted “Declan” just before Mr Berry lost control. The witnesses said Mr Berry shouted “oh shit” after the car hit a pothole and left the road. A nearby resident who witnessed the crash said he saw the headlights and rear lights “rotating through the air” but could not tell how they were rotating. He helped pull the survivors from the water, then searched the bank for the two missing occupants before emergency services arrived. Ms Gray said Cambridgeshire Highways had received 127 complaints about the road and that a survey four days before the crash found 98 potholes along North Brink. One near the crash site measured a quarter of the road’s width. The road was due to be repaired within 21 days, but the crash happened first. Highway workers filled the potholes the next day while the road was closed due to the incident. Ms Gray recorded a conclusion that Eden died in a road traffic accident, stating excessive speed was the main cause of the crash, and that the poor road surface had made more than a "minimal contribution" to the crash. She offered her condolences to Eden’s family members who were present: two aunts, an uncle and a cousin. Eden’s parents did not attend. An inquest into Declan Berry's death was heard yesterday.

metadata.title: Family describes horrific reality after teen's tragic death in Cambs river crash
metadata.contentSnippet: The family of a teenage girl killed in a river crash at Wisbech earlier this year have described the “horrific reality” they now face after an inquest into her death.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Family describes horrific reality after teen's tragic death in Cambs river crash
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The family of a teenage girl killed in a river crash at Wisbech earlier this year have described the “horrific reality” they now face after an inquest into her death. The hearing held today in Huntingdon heard that Eden Bunn, 16 and from Sutton Bridge, died as a result of a severe head injury suffered in the accident which happened on North Brink on March 17. Eden’s father Dean, mother Lisa, brother Jay and sister Shelby released the following statement after the inquest. “Eden was the kindest, most wonderful person and to have her snatched away from us so suddenly has left us heartbroken. "She was a beautiful soul and had such a love of life. No words can describe the devastation we feel and we will never get over losing her. "We don’t want to say anything about the lad who was driving. He has lost his life and his parents are going through the same living nightmare that we are. "Nothing will bring Eden back and her death is a horrific reality we will have to live with forever.” Sarah Townsend, a personal injury lawyer at Hodge Jones & Allen who represents the family, said: “Eden’s passing has understandably left her family inconsolable with grief and struggling to cope. "What is most tragic is that it was entirely avoidable and should serve as a warning to young drivers to not drive recklessly and put others at risk. "I hope that now the inquest process has concluded Eden’s family can slowly start to rebuild their lives.” The inquest heard that Eden was a rear seat passenger in a car driven by 18-year-old Declan Berry, from Wisbech, who also died in the accident, which was blamed on excessive speed, with potholes in the road a contributory factor. Another passenger in the car had told police the VW Polo had been going 90mph moments before the crash, which saw the vehicle leave the carriageway, roll down an embankment, before being fully submerged in the River Nene.

metadata.title: Six people complete 24-hour St Neots fitness challenge with 10,000 burpees
metadata.contentSnippet: Six people completed a gruelling 24-hour fitness challenge in St Neots.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Six people complete 24-hour St Neots fitness challenge with 10,000 burpees
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Six people completed a gruelling 24-hour fitness challenge in St Neots. The challenge, set by outdoor fitness group ABSolute Storm Fitness (Abstorm), included 25 back-to-back bootcamp sessions, 10,000 burpees, and a spin bike that ran non-stop for the full 24 hours. The event raised money for Ehlers-Danlos Support UK, Children’s Burns Camps and Parkinson’s UK. Abstorm founder and head coach Abi Black led all 25 sessions and oversaw the 10,000 burpees. Members of ABSolute Storm Fitness (Abstorm) who took part in the charity bootcamp (Image: Andy Clifton) Ms Black said: "We did it. "24 hours of bootcamps. "What a whirlwind of laughter and craziness, and so many memories. "I'm completely broken, but immensely proud. "This was our third year, our biggest year, and seeing six of our members pull off the full 24 hours non-stop is just unbelievable. "Abstorm isn't just a fitness group; we are a family and a core part of this community. "A massive thank you goes out to every single member who turned up to support, every person who jumped into a session, and everyone who has donated so far. "If you haven’t, please help us get to our total." Members of ABSolute Storm Fitness (Abstorm) who took part in the charity bootcamp (Image: Andy Clifton) The six participants, averaging 56, completed the entire challenge. The six were Ursula, 59, a Slimming World consultant; Ian, 57, a driving instructor; Nadine, 46, an environmental health officer; Sarah, 58, a geospatial analyst; Neil, 59, an aerospace and defence project manager; and Shaz, 58, a police force communications centre lead. They are the largest group to complete the full 24-hour challenge since the event began. Abstorm is aiming to raise a record £10,000 for the charities. Members of ABSolute Storm Fitness (Abstorm) who took part in the charity bootcamp (Image: Andy Clifton) The group promotes outdoor fitness in St Neots and nearby areas and welcomes members of all fitness levels. Sessions are held at Priory Park in St Neots and The Green in Brampton. The group's 2025 event raised more than £8,000—well above its £5,000 target—with support from more than 70 people who took part throughout the night.

metadata.title: Hospital redevelopment takes major step forward as land agreement reached
metadata.contentSnippet: Plans to redevelop a Hinchingbrooke Hospital have taken a major step forward.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hospital redevelopment takes major step forward as land agreement reached
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Plans to redevelop a hospital in Cambridgeshire have taken a major step forward. North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust has agreed in principle to acquire six hectares of land and associated highways. The acquisition of the former Cambridgeshire Police land marks a major step forward for the Hinchingbrooke Hospital redevelopment. Subject to planning consent, the land will allow for the creation of a new access road and 682 parking spaces. Environmental mitigation works and low-carbon energy infrastructure is also planned for the site. Hinchingbrooke Hospital was added to the New Hospital Programme in May 2023. The redevelopment programme is designed to address the challenges associated with ageing hospital infrastructure. Deborah Lee, senior responsible officer for Hinchingbrooke Hospital Redevelopment, said: "Reaching agreement on this land acquisition is a major milestone for the Hinchingbrooke Hospital Redevelopment Programme. "Securing this site will allow us to deliver the vital infrastructure needed to support our plans for a modern hospital that meets the needs of our patients, staff and communities for decades to come." Police and Crime Commissioner, Darryl Preston added: "As owner of the police estate in Cambridgeshire, I have a duty to ensure that land no longer needed for policing purposes is used in a way that delivers the greatest benefit to the public. "Once finalised, this sale will help improve access to local healthcare facilities, providing a positive outcome for residents and the wider community." Have you got a story you want to share? He was seen running towards Church Street and is described as wearing blue jeans, a black top, a baseball cap, and a snood covering his face. Two men dressed in black and wearing balaclavas arrived in a black vehicle, smashed the front window. They stole a bag of cigarettes before fleeing towards Green Street. summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A paedophile from Cambridgeshire who messaged people he believed were children and arranged to meet them has been jailed. Timothy Pavitt, 73, was brought to police attention after he uploaded indecent images of children to a Kik account in 2024. Officers were able to trace the IP address of the account, which led them to Pavitt’s home in Boxworth End, Swavesey. He was arrested on February 19, 2025, and claimed in interview to be “lonely” and using chat sites to speak to children and download images. A review of his devices found he had been speaking in a sexual manner with users he believed to be children and arranging to meet up with them. The devices also contained more than 350 indecent images. The identities of the people he was messaging have never been confirmed. Pavitt was jailed for four years and eight months at Peterborough Crown Court on Monday September 21. He had previously admitted to 18 counts, including communicating sexually with children and making indecent images. He was also handed an indefinite sexual harm prevention order (SHPO). Det Sgt Zip Lloyd said: "Pavitt knew what he was doing was wrong but continued to seek out users he believed were children, encourage sexual conversations and make indecent images. "He was also actively sharing those images for others to view, further fuelling the exploitation of children. I am pleased he is now behind bars. "Protecting young people from harm is one of our top priorities and we will continue to work tirelessly to keep children safe." Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: The hardest secondary schools to get into in Cambridgeshire revealed
metadata.contentSnippet: The hardest secondary schools to get into in Cambridgeshire have been revealed as parents and carers decide where their children will study next year.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The hardest secondary schools to get into in Cambridgeshire revealed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The hardest secondary schools to get into have been revealed as parents and carers decide where their children will study next year. The window for applications for pupils starting year 7 in September 2027 opened earlier this month and will run until October 31. Last year, 7,050 students found out where they’d be heading with 96.7 per cent securing a place at one of their first, second or third preference schools. The hardest school to get into was Chesterton Community College, with enough places for just 60 per cent of children who put it down as their first preference. Earlier this year, the school was listed as the top performing school in the county – with 83.7 per cent of pupils achieving a Grade 5 or higher in their English and maths GCSEs. In its latest Ofsted report the school was also found to be outstanding in every category, with the inspector finding it has an “extremely high level of ambition for all pupils” which is matched by the pupils’ “own determination to succeed”. St Bede’s Inter-Church School in Cambridge was the second hardest to get into with 190 places for 301 first-place preferences – a success rate of 63 per cent. Soham Village College was ranked third with 78 per cent of pupils successfully admitted to 270 places from 247 first-place preferences. Parents and carers of children about to enter secondary school can submit their applications for places on the county council website. They have until the national closing date of October 31, after which late applications will be considered once all on-time applications are determined. A Cambridgeshire County Council spokesperson said: “This year in Cambridgeshire 96.6 per cent of children were offered a place at either their first, second or third preference schools, this is above national benchmarks. Notably, both this year and last year, 5 per cent more children in Cambridgeshire received an offer from their first preference school than did nationally. “We’re committed to providing the best possible start in life for young people in our county and access to high quality education close to home is key. With population centres changing over time around our growing county, the council’s Education team work hard, in partnership with schools and with careful reference to pupil forecasting figures, to try and ensure we can offer the right numbers of school places, in the right areas, when they are needed.”

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire campaign could unlock £2m a year in unclaimed Pension Credit
metadata.contentSnippet: A campaign could put up to £2 million a year back in the pockets of older Cambridgeshire residents.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire campaign could unlock £2m a year in unclaimed Pension Credit
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A campaign could put up to £2 million a year back in the pockets of older Cambridgeshire residents. More than 700 households across Cambridgeshire will be contacted about unclaimed Pension Credit in a joint council campaign. The campaign is the county’s first targeted campaign to increase residents’ income since approval of the procurement of the Low-Income Family Tracker (LIFT) software platform at a meeting of the County Council’s Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee in February, funded through the UK Government’s Crisis and Resilience Fund via the DWP. Alison Whelan, chair of the Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee at Cambridgeshire County Council, said: "This new targeted campaign will boost financial security and quality of life for hundreds of families across our county. "I’m delighted to know that in Cambridgeshire we’re putting money, up to £2M, back in the pockets of the families that are most vulnerable to the cost-of-living pressures facing us nationally. "Please help us to spread the word about this excellent campaign so that families contacted by their district or city council will know they can trust the information they’ve been given – it’s good news!" Eligible residents will be contacted directly by their local council: Cambridge City, East Cambridgeshire, South Cambridgeshire, Huntingdonshire or Fenland. Councils will contact residents by letter, email or phone. Pension Credit comes in two parts: Guarantee Credit and Savings Credit. Some households may be eligible for both. The council estimates the 500 identified households could gain more than £2 million a year if they all claim Guarantee Credit, based on an average award of £4,300. No scams have been reported in connection with the campaign. The campaign follows a 2024 council motion calling for a proactive campaign to ensure eligible pensioners were informed about Pension Credit after changes to winter fuel payments.

metadata.title: Mayor backs Ely City FC with personal sponsorship and solar plans debated
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambs Mayor Paul Bristow answered questions from the public during a recent event held at Ely City Football Club.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Mayor backs Ely City FC with personal sponsorship and solar plans debated
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambs Mayor Paul Bristow answered questions from the public during a recent event held in Ely - here's what happened Last Thursday evening (September 17), keen football supporter and mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, Paul Bristow, was in his element when he held the third of his Question Time events at Ely City Football Club. And the charismatic chair of the football club, Alan Alsop, was a member of the audience, as host Paul Brackley, editor of the Cambridge Independent, asked the questions sent in prior that were all answered knowledgeably and in depth. He spoke about everything from the state of Fen roads to the siting of dropped kerbs, resolving water problems in south Cambridgeshire, to new building and proposed destruction of swathes of rural flora and fauna for a ‘busway’—a scheme with which he expressed his disapproval—to broader issues like the restructuring of councils. Paul Bristow answers many questions (Image: Cathy Gibb de Swarte) Mr Bristow also answered some lively questions from the floor—and mentioned he would be visiting Littleport this week, as well as his interest in the town’s history. Before leaving the club, which supports 33 teams, he discovered that both businesses and individuals can sponsor games for £80. This includes six guest tickets and refreshments in a hospitality framework. He then told chairman Alan that he was going to do just that personally. Alan then told the Mayor that he was going to look at the council grant scheme for installing solar panels on the roof of the club premises. Paul Bristow has served as the strategic authority mayor for Cambridgeshire and Peterborough since 2025. Prior to that he was the Member of Parliament for Peterborough, where he was brought up and still lives, from 2019 until 2024. In his introduction, he said: “Mayors have an increasingly important role in shaping the future of our communities, from improving transport and supporting local businesses to delivering new homes and creating opportunities for growth.”

metadata.title: Probe into care of man accused of throwing boy into crocodile pit continues
metadata.contentSnippet: Norfolk County Council has confirmed it continues to investigate the care given to a man accused of throwing a toddler into a crocodile pit.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Probe into care of man accused of throwing boy into crocodile pit continues
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council has confirmed it continues to probe the care given to a disabled man accused of throwing a toddler into a crocodile pit. Norfolk County Council opened a safeguarding inquiry after the three-year-old boy was injured at Johnsons of Old Hurst, near Huntingdon, on June 18. He was rescued from the pit by staff members, including the zoo's owners Andy and Tracey Johnson, who are said to have leapt into the enclosure. It has was later revealed the toddler was attacked by one of the reptiles and he has since been discharged after spending more than a month in hospital. A 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and released on bail (Image: Newsquest) A 30-year-old man from Norfolk was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after the boy sustained serious injuries. He was released on bail until September 18 but has since been re-bailed by police until December 17. A source with knowledge of the situation claimed the man, believed to have learning difficulties, was visiting the zoo with two carers. It is alleged the carers left the crocodile enclosure with the suspect after the incident but were unable to leave the grounds after staff members intervened. Other witnesses claimed the carers were "on their phones" and "weren't paying him much attention". Police declared a critical incident after the toddler sustained serious injuries (Image: Joe Giddens/PA) Council officials confirmed it was investigating whether the man is being neglected or abused while in care. The county council revealed it had launched a Section 42 inquiry and stopped referrals to the care provider in the suspect's case. These require local authorities to investigate when they suspect an adult receiving care is experiencing, or at risk of, abuse or neglect. While the suspect is from the county, his care was not commissioned, provided or paid for by the council. In an update issued on Monday (September 21), Norfolk County Council said it continues to work with partner organisations. Norfolk County Council confirmed it was investigating whether the man is being neglected or abused while in care. (Image: Joe Giddens/PA) A spokesperson said: "This was a deeply distressing incident and our thoughts remain with the individual and their family. "While Norfolk County Council was not involved in providing, commissioning or funding the care concerned, we take our safeguarding responsibilities seriously and continue to work in collaboration with relevant partner organisations to ensure appropriate safeguarding processes are followed. "As enquiries remain ongoing, it would not be appropriate to comment further on an individual case." The three-year-old boy has since been discharged from hospital (Image: SWNS) Johnsons of Old Hurst described the incident as "one of the most distressing" in its history. The zoo thanked visitors who "stepped forward to help," including off-duty paramedics and police officers. summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire man who sent abusive, degrading and racist messages to an England international footballer has avoided prison. Brian Bealey, 69, posted multiple public comments on social media platform X between March 17 and 29. The messages were directed at England and then-Tottenham Hotspur player Djed Spence. Cambridgeshire Police's Football Policing Officer worked alongside the UK Football Policing Unit to identify Bealey. It follows a referral from the Football Association and Premier League after England’s fixture against Uruguay on March 27. Investigators linked the X account used to send the messages to Bealey, of Main Street, Witchford, Ely. The messages contained racially offensive language and slurs directed at Spence, who now plays for Inter Milan. They were also directed at other individuals, and were assessed as grossly offensive and racially aggravated. At Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on Thursday (September 17), Bealey pleaded guilty to sending by public communication offensive messages. He was fined £1,000. Detective Sergeant Dominic Carminati, who investigated, said: "There is absolutely no place for racism, either in football or in society as a whole. "Djed Spence was subjected to a series of offensive, degrading and racially aggravated messages that were intended to cause distress and spread hatred online. "People often believe they can hide behind anonymous social media accounts, but this case demonstrates that those who use online platforms to target others with racist abuse can and will be identified. "We would encourage anyone who experiences or witnesses racist abuse online to report it to the platform involved and to police." Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Amazon warehouse plans could create more than 2,300 jobs
metadata.contentSnippet: Amazon's proposed Biggleswade warehouse could create 2,300 jobs, with plans for 166,000sqm at Stratton Business Park and A1 traffic changes in Bedfordshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Amazon warehouse plans could create more than 2,300 jobs
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. More than 2,300 jobs could be created through plans for an Amazon warehouse in Biggleswade, according to a councillor. A planning application has been submitted by the world’s largest online retailer to Central Bedfordshire Council for the premises on the town’s Stratton Business Park, said Conservative Biggleswade East councillor Grant Fage on social media. These employment opportunities would cover a range of roles, he posted on Facebook. “The warehouse would be accompanied by three extra units, while the site is expected to include 166,000sqm of floor space. “The company’s proposals include changes to the A1 south roundabout, including traffic lights on the approaches from both north and south. “This is a very complicated application and will have huge impacts on Biggleswade, positively in terms of job creation but negatively for our road network. “In the recent Central Bedfordshire Local Plan consultation, this site was referenced both in my response and that of Biggleswade Town Council, as being a site that could support commercial development in certain circumstances. “Having seen this application, I’ve no objection but would ask that the following commitments are honoured in full: “The reconfiguration of the A1 roundabout is needed, but it’s sub-optimal to have traffic signals.” Councillor Fage wondered if National Highways could be asked to confirm “whether traffic lights are absolutely necessary” on both the northern and southern approaches. “We need that independent view,” he explained. “If National Highways says traffic signals are required, I hope it highlights the desperate state of the A1 in Biggleswade. “We’d have the only traffic lights on the entire A1 stretch between South Mimms and Scotland. This didn’t work for the Black Cat roundabout and it feels like a step backwards. “The queues at Pegasus Drive are very challenging now for drivers exiting Stratton Business Park. Traffic lights east of the Lidl mini-roundabout makes sense, although further efforts are needed to remove bottle necks. “That would include as cars exit Lidl, while yellow lines are needed along both sides of Lancaster Way.” Reacting to his post, Biggleswade town councillor Mark Knight warned: “Installing (traffic) lights on the A1 roundabout is madness. “Planners are repeating the history of short-term thinking that was used for decades at the Black Cat roundabout.” Amazon made a shock announcement in January to close its Marston Gate centre at Ridgmont, opting for a new site in Northampton. Almost 600 employees were based at the company’s first UK site, and it was one of Central Bedfordshire’s biggest employers since opening in 1999. Central Bedfordshire Council’s development management committee is expected to consider the project in due course.

metadata.title: 'Excessive speed' and potholes blamed for fatal Wisbech river crash inquest told
metadata.contentSnippet: Wisbech teenager Declan Berry drowned after his car hit a pothole at 90mph and plunged into the River Nene, an inquest heard. Sixteen-year-old Eden Bunn also died.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Excessive speed' and potholes blamed for fatal Wisbech river crash inquest told
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Wisbech teenager Declan Berry drowned after his car hit a pothole at 90mph and plunged into the River Nene, an inquest heard. The teenage driver was told to slow down moments before his car plunged into the water, killing him and sixteen-year-old rear passenger, Eden Bunn. Mr Berry, 18, was travelling at around 90mph when his Volkswagen Polo hit a pothole on North Brink, Wisbech, and rolled down an embankment into the river, the hearing heard. Declan Berry's family and friends laid tributes and waited for news as searches of the River Nene were carried out for his body. (Image: Sarah Cliss) None of his family was at the hearing at Vantage House in Huntingdon, which was conducted by written statements, and heard that Mr Berry drowned after the March 17 crash; his body was recovered from the river nearly two weeks later at the town’s marina. A police officer called to identify the body confirmed it was Mr Berry due to an unusual tattoo on the back of his neck and his clothing. Police investigator James Mills concluded that speed was the main factor in the crash, while the pothole-riddled road, with crumbling edges and an uneven surface, also contributed. Cambridgeshire area coroner Elizabeth Gray read the evidence from the various witnesses about the crash, which happened at around 8.19pm as Mr Berry drove four teenage friends along North Brink, away from the town centre. The front-seat passenger told police he had looked at the speedometer and that Mr Berry was driving at 90mph moments before the crash and he had asked him to slow down. Mr Berry replied, "It will be all right", before the car hit a pothole and he lost control. Eden Bunn, 16, died after the car she was travelling in entered the River Nene, near Wisbech (Image: Cambridgeshire) The unnamed 18-year-old witness said Mr Berry tried to control the car before shouting: "Oh shit" as the car left the road, rolled several times and plunged into the river. The witness said he met Mr Berry at McDonald’s, accepted an invitation to go for a drive and believed Mr Berry had "intended to show off". He escaped through the broken passenger window and described the water around him as dark, telling officers he did not know where the others were as he made his escape. Declan Berry's body was recovered from Wisbech Marina nearly two weeks after the fatal crash. (Image: Alan Berry) A female passenger sitting behind the front passenger, who was not wearing a seat belt, recalled a near miss on the same stretch of road a week earlier. The other unnamed second rear-seat passenger, who was sat behind Mr Berry, heard a thud beneath the car but did not know what it struck before it rolled into the water. She struggled to release her seat belt before escaping through a broken window and being rescued by members of the public. One of the women had also told police that she was used to Mr Berry driving at speed, and it was what she expected. Many floral tributes were left by the River Nene in Wisbech following the horrific crash. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Eden Bunn from Sutton Bridge was sitting in the middle and had reportedly called out "Declan" moments before the crash. Her inquest is due tomorrow. An eyewitness on his driveway at the time of the crash heard a vehicle approach at speed before a loud bang. He saw the headlights and rear lights "rotating through the air", then ran and found the vehicle completely submerged. He asked his partner to call emergency services before helping those involved, who had made it to the bank but needed help out of the water. A Cambridgeshire Search & Rescue team were at the scene for several days. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Mr Mills’ report found a steering defect and suspension modifications on the VW, but no evidence that either contributed to the crash. Investigators recovered a dashcam and black box from the Polo, but neither contained any data. Cambridgeshire County Council recorded 98 potholes during a survey just days before the accident and set a 21-day deadline for repairs, but the crash happened first. Repairs were carried out immediately after the crash, while the road was closed as a result of the incident. The accident report said speed was the main factor: it left the driver less time to react to potholes before he lost control. At a lower speed, the rollover would have been less severe. Ms Gray concluded that Mr Berry drowned after a single-vehicle crash. She concluded that "excessive speed", the road conditions, and the poor surface more than likely contributed to his death.

metadata.title: Cambs primary school praised for 'welcoming' environment in Ofsted report
metadata.contentSnippet: Earith Primary School has been praised for its "welcoming and nurturing" environment in its latest Ofsted report.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs primary school praised for 'welcoming' environment in Ofsted report
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Huntingdonshire primary school has been praised for its "welcoming and nurturing" environment in its latest Ofsted report. Earith Primary School near Huntingdon, part of the Active Learning Trust, was inspected on July 14 and met the expected standard overall, with early years and personal development judged strong. Inspectors said pupils feel safe and well supported in a “welcoming and nurturing” school where they enjoy positive relationships with staff and each other. Ofsted also praised the school for tailoring parts of its curriculum to the local community. Because the school is surrounded by waterways, pupils receive extra water-safety lessons, while older children learn about healthy relationships, artificial intelligence, digital footprints and online misinformation. Duncan Low, Director of Learning at Active Learning Trust, said: “We are very pleased to see Ofsted inspectors recognise the strengths and achievements at Earith Primary School and the positive experience it provides for pupils and their families. The school is located near Huntingdon (Image: Earith Primary School) “We know that the school plays a hugely important role at the heart of the village community in Earith and would like to thank the staff for all the hard work and commitment that they bring every day." Inspectors said pupils build a strong understanding of different cultures, religions and beliefs through the school council, voting and debates about democracy. Every pupil has a responsibility in the school community, helping them build independence and leadership skills. The report also highlighted extra-curricular opportunities including sporting events, educational visits, music activities and residential trips. Inspectors noted that pupils develop a strong understanding of different cultures (Image: Earith Primary School) Pupils particularly value the on-site swimming pool, which inspectors said is important because of the school’s location. Most pupils achieved in line with national expectations, made appropriate progress and were well prepared for the next stage of education. Attendance was above the national average, including among disadvantaged pupils and those with special educational needs and/or disabilities. Headteacher Thomas Abbs said: “I am delighted that this Ofsted report recognises the warm, welcoming and inclusive environment we work so hard to achieve at our village school. Attendance rates were found to be above national averages (Image: Earith Primary School) “The report is a strong endorsement of the hard work of our staff and pupils, as well as the support of our families, and of the wonderful sense of community that makes our school such a special place. “We look forward to building on this excellent report as we continue to provide the very best opportunities for our children.” Ofsted said that leaders should continue to strengthen curriculum evaluation to ensure pupils consistently gain and apply intended knowledge and skills across all subjects. Inspectors also recommended further support to help pupils manage their emotions and behaviour more independently.

Kite Trust team members Financial pressure has already forced the charity to cut support groups and suspend major community events, including its popular Queer Prom. summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Huntingdon Scouts could finally have a permanent home after years on the move. The group has secured a 30-year lease on a former maintenance building on St Peters Road, ending years of operating without a fixed base and regularly moving equipment between different borrowed spaces. They now plan to turn the industrial site into a dedicated scouting centre. Steve Harris, who is leading the project, said: "Having a permanent home means we can spend less time moving gear and more time providing life-changing adventures for our young people. This building represents a 30-year commitment to the youth and the people of Huntingdon." Huntingdon Scouts are part of the Scout Association, helping young people build life skills through camping, hiking, crafts and community service. The centre will include a main activity hall, modern meeting rooms, a kitchen, toilets and other amenities. The group also hopes the centre will become a community hub. The team wants other organisations to use the centre, helping tackle a shortage of quality community venues in the area. But turning the old building into a modern community hub will cost money. Several grants have been secured, but more money is needed to finish the project. Huntingdon Scouts are appealing to residents and businesses for donations, sponsorship, materials and labour. A group spokesperson said: "Every bit of help will go directly toward creating a lasting legacy for the town. The Scouts are inviting anyone who can offer money or professional services to get in touch." Anyone who can help should email info@hinchingbrookescouts.org or visit the Huntingdon Scout Centre Facebook page. The planned conversion is set to take place in three phases, starting with basic repairs before adding an accessible toilet and wet room, followed by enhancements for youth groups and other community users.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More than 75 people flocked to a sold-out Huntingdon talk on the dark history of witch trials. The event was part of this year’s Heritage Open Days in Huntingdonshire and was organised by Huntingdon Town Council and The Cromwell Museum. The talk, led by Cromwell Museum curator Stuart Orme, was moved from the Court Room to the larger Assembly Room, but extra tickets quickly sold out. Stuart said: "The Huntingdonshire Witch Trials are one of the most intriguing aspects of our local history, so it has been wonderful to see so many people wanting to learn more about the people and events behind the story. "Whilst Heritage Open Days shines a spotlight on our shared heritage, the Cromwell Museum is free to visit throughout the year, and I would encourage anyone with an interest in Huntingdon's past to come along and discover more of the remarkable stories our town has to tell." Guided Walk at Priory Road Cemetary (Image: Huntingdon Town Council) The talk covered the region’s witch-trial history, including the Witches of Warboys, the infamous Witchfinder General Matthew Hopkins and Huntingdon woman Mary Hicks, who may have been the last person executed for witchcraft in England, although both her existence and that claim are disputed. The witch-trials talk was part of a wider Heritage Open Days programme that included an open day at Priory Road Cemetery and Chapel, where visitors explored burial records and learned about former Huntingdon Burial Board members. The programme will conclude with two fully booked guided tours of Huntingdon Town Hall, giving attendees the chance to explore the town’s civic heritage. The Cromwell Museum and self-guided trails from the Discover Huntingdon Visitor Centre offer residents and visitors year-round ways to explore the town’s history. Huntingdon saw witchcraft trials in 1593, 1646 and 1716, with at least four people hanged at Mill Common after the 1646 proceedings.

metadata.title: Small changes urged as Zero Waste Week highlights how to rethink rubbish
metadata.contentSnippet: Martin Cooper, owner of The Refill Shop of Ikigai in St Ives, writes his latest column.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Small changes urged as Zero Waste Week highlights how to rethink rubbish
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Martin Cooper, owner of The Refill Shop of Ikigai in St Ives, writes his latest column It's time to rethink our rubbish. Do you know how much waste you produce on a weekly basis? With more bins being rolled out from the council, it’s hard to keep track of just how much we are throwing away, but Zero Waste Week is an opportunity to take notice. Zero Waste Week was held between September 7 and 11 and has become a regular in the calendar of environmental campaigns to help us reduce what we throw away. But why does it matter? Carry reusable items (Image: Martin Cooper) The scale of our waste problem is easy to overlook because most of it disappears the moment the bin lorry pulls away. We generate millions of tonnes of rubbish every year, most of which ends up in landfill rather than being reused or recycled. Landfill sites take up valuable land, can leach pollutants into soil and waterways and represent a huge waste of the energy and resources that went into making the products in the first place. Every takeaway container, unopened food packet or old appliance thrown away is a small loss multiplied by millions of households doing the same thing. Rather than demanding perfection – which we know will never be achieved, Zero Waste Week encourages us to pick one habit and try to improve it for seven days – then keep going until it sticks. And it’s not as hard as you might think: You can audit your bins – during Zero Waste Week, make note of what you throw away most – awareness alone often changes behaviour. Cut your food waste by planning meals, freezing leftovers and using up odds and ends before they spoil – food waste is one of the easiest and most impactful areas to tackle. Choose reusables – swap single-use bags, bottles and cutlery for versions you can use again and again. Repair, don’t replace – Huntingdonshire has a number of repair cafés throughout the year, that can fix clothes, electronics, and furniture that might otherwise be binned, and the Sew, Mend and Repair group, who meet in St Ives, help repair and alter clothes to keep them going. Buy loose and local – reducing packaging by shopping at markets or refill shops will cut your waste before it even reaches your home – and gives you an opportunity to reuse what you already have. Zero Waste Week won’t solve the waste crisis on its own, but small, collective changes add up. This September, it’s worth asking “what’s one thing I could throw away less of?”.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Little Paxton Lawn Cemetery has been recognised for its care and presentation. The Little Paxton Parish Council-owned cemetery won a Silver Award in the BRAMM Cemetery of the Year Awards. The award recognises the team’s upkeep and care in creating a peaceful place for families to remember loved ones. Kathy Bishop, chairperson of Little Paxton Parish Council, said: “We are delighted to receive the BRAMM Cemetery of the Year Silver Award. “This award demonstrates the hard work, care and attention given by our council maintenance team. “The cemetery is an important and much-loved part of Little Paxton, and we are incredibly proud that the dedication of our Team has been recognised through this award.” The BRAMM Cemetery of the Year Awards recognise those who keep cemeteries to a high standard. The parish council thanked its maintenance team for keeping the cemetery cared for and presentable throughout the year. The cemetery was also extended by 2.2 acres, with the new area expected to provide sufficient burial space for the next 50 years and accommodate double-depth graves.

metadata.title: Young anglers catch and return 723 fish in confidence-building summer programme
metadata.contentSnippet: A summer fishing programme has helped young people in Huntingdonshire build confidence, improve their wellbeing and learn new skills.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Young anglers catch and return 723 fish in confidence-building summer programme
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A summer fishing programme has helped young people in Huntingdonshire build confidence, improve their wellbeing and learn new skills. The Dreamdrops Fishing Programme, run by children’s charity Dreamdrops in partnership with the Fly-Fishing Academy, took place every Tuesday in August at Rectory Farm in Great Addington, Northamptonshire. Up to eight young anglers attended each session, including graduates of an earlier life-skills angling course and two working towards the Angling Skills Activity Award. Roger Adams, an instructor from the Fly-Fishing Academy, said: "Where did August go? "It’s been tremendous fun, but my life has flashed before me – I have lost four weeks of it!" Richard Winser of the Fly-Fishing Academy said: "There have been some great sessions, they seemed to get incrementally better each time we ventured out; angling appeals on so many different levels and in so many personal ways, to different people. George Ward (Image: Dreamdrops Children's Charity) "It can enhance wellbeing and be very therapeutic just being outside and around water, in a safe and controlled environment." The young anglers caught and safely returned 723 fish during the programme. George Ward, a current participant, said: "I liked the way that the instructors had loads of time for you, and you didn’t feel rushed. "Everything was explained simply and they always told us what would be covered next. "The Zoom tutorials and Kahoot quizzes were serious fun. "It was great to have such a good course structure, and I learnt loads of new and different fishing techniques – amazing." Parent Michelle Quail praised the programme. She said: "For us personally, the fishing days have been such good fun and have stood out as a highlight of our summer, it has given us an opportunity to do things we would otherwise not have had a chance to do and to make some really lovely family memories along the way." Dreamdrops committee chair Christine Luckham congratulated the two young anglers who completed the course and will receive Gold Award Level certificates at a ceremony at Huntingdon Town Hall on September 12. She also thanked the Fly-Fishing Academy team, saying: "Once again, my thanks to the Fly-Fishing Academy team who have ploughed a new furrow and extended the boundaries further for our fishing programme and angling initiative." The Angling Skills Activity Award - Foundation (Gold) course includes three online tutorials and four additional fishing days, with participants required to demonstrate competency in 17 areas.

metadata.title: Hunts care home goes from 'requires improvement' to 'good' in latest inspection
metadata.contentSnippet: Montague House care home in Brampton has been rated good overall after previously requiring improvement by the Care Quality Commission (CQC).

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts care home goes from 'requires improvement' to 'good' in latest inspection
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Huntingdonshire care home has been rated good overall after previously being judged to require improvement by the Care Quality Commission (CQC). Montague House, in Keeling Lane, Brampton, was assessed between July 30 and August 19, with the report published September 8. The home provides accommodation, nursing and personal care for 52 residents, including people living with dementia. Montague House was awarded ‘Good’ ratings across four out of five criteria (Safe, Effective, Responsive and Well-led) and an 'Outstanding' rating for Caring. At the previous inspection in March 2023, inspectors found the provider breached regulations on safe care, treatment and governance. The CQC said the provider had made “sufficient improvements” and was no longer breaching the regulations. The care home no longer 'requires improvement' (Image: Montague House) Home Manager Paula Yorkston Toy said: “We are delighted with the CQC report and to have received an ‘Outstanding’ rating in ‘Caring’. “I want to thank every member of the team here for helping us to achieve this result and for their contribution to Montague House. “The residents and their wellbeing are at the heart of everything we do, and it’s terrific that the inspectors have recognised our dedication and care.” The latest inspection report reads: "People experienced personalised care from staff who understood them well and supported them to live meaningful and fulfilling lives. "Staff demonstrated a detailed understanding of people's individual needs, preferences and life histories. "There were many examples of compassionate, person-centred care, particularly for people living with dementia." Montague House in Brampton was rated 'good' in its latest inspection (Image: Montague House) Inspectors identified areas for further work, including safeguarding recognition and reporting, records showing repositioning had taken place as assessed, care planning and medicines oversight. There was no evidence of avoidable harm and the provider responded positively to feedback and took action. Residents took part in activities, therapies and community links, including exercise programmes, dementia activities and religious services. Inspectors found visible, approachable leaders and a positive culture at the home. Inspectors said residents had positive experiences, with staff acting calmly, patiently and respectfully and adapting to their emotional and wellbeing needs. A person told inspectors: "I like it here and I'm happy to be here."

metadata.title: 10 of the best independent restaurants in Cambridgeshire you need to try
metadata.contentSnippet: These independent restaurants and gastropubs in Cambridgeshire are some of the best-rated by online reviewers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 10 of the best independent restaurants in Cambridgeshire you need to try
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire's food scene is unrivalled, with hundreds of hidden gems and independent restaurants well worth a visit. Here are 10 of the best independent restaurants in the county that you need to try, with glowing reviews from previous visitors. The Cock is an award-winning country pub and restaurant. It has won the national dining pub title twice and serves seasonal British menus in a riverside village setting. It has more than 700 "excellent" reviews on TripAdvisor. This independent hotel restaurant in Huntingdon is known for modern British cooking, an excellent wine list and its riverside location. It has an overall rating of 4.5 out of five stars on TripAdvisor with more than 800 reviews. The Crown Inn is a highly regarded village gastropub. It is particularly noted for seasonal British food and is popular with local diners and food enthusiasts. One reviewer wrote: "We have just had our wedding at The Crown and we cannot praise the place and the team there highly enough. "They are attentive professional and diligent. The food is absolutely amazing." This independent Italian restaurant overlooking the river is one of the town’s best-rated restaurants and is suited to special occasions and date nights. One five-star review reads: "We dined on excellent pasta dishes which although not inexpensive turned out to be great value based on the high quality of the ingredients and lovely slightly old fashioned surroundings and atmosphere." The Old Fire Engine House in Ely is an independent restaurant and gallery established in 1968. It uses local and seasonal ingredients and is one of the city’s most iconic dining destinations. It has more than 600 "excellent" reviews on TripAdvisor. Eat Thai is a small independent restaurant in Ely, frequently cited among the town’s best eateries. One five-star review reads: "Everything was first class, fresh ingredients cooked perfectly with very friendly, helpful staff and very reasonable prices." The Lamb & Flag in Welney is among Fenland’s best-rated gastropubs. It is particularly renowned for Sunday lunches and has consistently strong customer reviews. On TripAdvisor, it is ranked first out of 96 restaurants in Wisbech. Oliver Twist Restaurant is an independent family-run restaurant in Guyhirn. It has an excellent local reputation and serves quality British cuisine. The country inn has more than 100 "excellent" reviews on TripAdvisor. The Red Lion in Wisbech is one of the best-rated independent restaurants in the town. It is popular for traditional British cooking and Sunday roasts. One five-star review reads: "Such a warm, welcoming atmosphere — I’ll definitely be back and only wish I’d found it sooner." Worzals in Wisbech St Mary is a landmark Fenland restaurant with a farm-to-fork focus. It is popular for celebratory meals and Sunday lunches. One visitor wrote on TripAdvisor: "Absolutely perfect roast dinner. I've been out for a lot of roast dinner in my time and this has got to be the best! "Lovely size meals perfect amount of meat for the roasts."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A 20-year-old has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a man died in a crash involving a car and an e-bike. Police were called to the collision on Dallow Road, Luton, at around 10.50pm on September 18. Officers found a man with serious injuries believed to have been struck by a vehicle. Emergency services attended to him but he was pronounced dead shortly after. A man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of murder and remains in custody for questioning. The Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Major Crime Unit has launched a murder investigation and is appealing for any witnesses, or people with CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage, to come forward. Bedfordshire Police also urged social media users not to share videos of the incident online and instead contact police, as it could be vital evidence. Anyone with information is asked to visit the police website, contact Crimestoppers or call 101, quoting Operation Stormwell.

metadata.title: Passengers warned of rail disruption after electricity fault
metadata.contentSnippet: Passengers are facing rail disruption after an electricity supply failure which has reduced services between Stevenage and Finsbury Park.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Passengers warned of rail disruption after electricity fault
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Passengers are facing rail disruption after an electricity supply failure. The fault occurred in the Welwyn area and has reduced the number of services running between Stevenage and Finsbury Park. National Rail said services between Stevenage and London could be cancelled, changed or delayed by up to 20 minutes. Electricity suppliers and Network Rail are working to restore power, but disruption is expected until at least 3pm, National Rail said. The incident was first reported at 3.22am on Friday (September 18) and has affected several routes. Thameslink and Great Northern passengers are expected to face disruption throughout the morning. Customers have been advised to allow at least 45 extra minutes to travel and may need to catch a different train. Great Northern will run fewer trains between Cambridge and London. However, tickets will be accepted on Thameslink trains to London St Pancras International and Great Northern trains to London King's Cross. Passengers can also use Greater Anglia trains to London Liverpool Street at no extra cost, National Rail said. Great Northern will also run a reduced peak-time service between Peterborough and London King's Cross as well as Hertford North and Moorgate. LNER passengers can also use their tickets on Avanti West Coast, Great Northern and Thameslink trains. More information, including an alternative route map and details of ticket acceptance, is available on the operator's website. Have you got a story you want to share? summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire jewellers has been forced to close after being targeted in their second break-in in less than a year. Police were called to Chloe's Jewellers in March at 8.30am on Wednesday, September 16. The force arrived by 9am and a police spokesperson conformed a crime has been raised for business burglary. Investigations are ongoing. The family-owned jeweller has been trading for more than 100 years and has stores across East Anglia, including in St Ives, Wisbech and Royston. Police were called to the St Ives branch at just before 3.30am on April 30 to reports of the front window being smashed and thousands of pounds worth of jewellery being stolen. Joe Ross, of Hawkins Road, Cambridge, was jailed for 16 months at Peterborough Crown Court on August 26 after admitting smashing into a shop and stealing £29,000 worth of jewellery. The March branch will now be temporarily closed following the recent break-in.

metadata.title: Iconic pop band Madness to headline 2027 outdoor festival near Cambs
metadata.contentSnippet: Iconic pop band Madness are set to headline 2027 Forest Live at shows near Cambridgeshire, with special guests Scouting For Girls.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Iconic pop band Madness to headline 2027 outdoor festival near Cambs
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Iconic pop band Madness are set to headline a 2027 festival near Cambridgeshire, with special guests Scouting For Girls. The four Forest Live summer shows, organised by Forestry England and promoter Cuffe & Taylor, will take place in Delamere, Thetford, Cannock Chase and Westonbirt Arboretum in June 2027. Madness last headlined Forest Live in 2005 and will return to the stage in 2027. Madness, known for hits including Our House and Baggy Trousers, have had 15 Top 10 singles during a career spanning more than 40 years. Last year, they released Hit Parade, a 45-track anthology celebrating 45 years of music. Madness said: "From the early days to the latest tracks... we've packed up the lot and brought them all together in Hit Parade. "It's a proper nutty collection of our biggest and best. "Press play, turn it up, and enjoy the ride." The collection includes 27 Top 40 hits, including It Must Be Love, Lovestruck and chart-topper House of Fun. A new 4K restoration of their 1981 film Take It Or Leave It will be shown in cinemas in October. More than 2.5 million people have attended Forest Live concerts over the past 25 years. The series brings live music to outdoor settings while helping fund forestry work across the country. A spokesperson for Forestry England said: "We manage and care for the nation’s 1,500 woods and forests. "We use the money Forest Live raises to maintain these beautiful natural areas for everyone to enjoy, run important conservation projects and keep growing trees." Scouting For Girls will support Madness on the night. Formed in London in 2005, Scouting For Girls have sold more than two million albums and singles, earned four Brit Award nominations and scored a string of radio hits. They have also sold out shows at Wembley Arena and the Royal Albert Hall, plus two nights at the London Palladium. The Forest Live 2027 dates are: • Saturday, June 19, 2027 – Delamere Forest • Sunday, June 20, 2027 – High Lodge, Thetford Forest • Saturday, June 26, 2027 – Cannock Chase Forest • Sunday, June 27, 2027 – Westonbirt Arboretum Tickets for all shows go on general sale at 10am on Friday, September 25, through forestlive.com. Fans can also sign up through the website for updates, announcements and exclusive pre-sale access.

metadata.title: 'Predator' raped woman in horrific late-night attack near filling station
metadata.contentSnippet: A "dangerous" predator who raped a woman in a late-night attack near the BP filling station on Lynn Road, in Wisbech, has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Predator' raped woman in horrific late-night attack near filling station
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A "dangerous" predator who raped a woman in a late-night attack near a Cambridgeshire filling station has been jailed for seven years. Darius Andrulionis, 46, began speaking to the victim near the BP filling station, in Lynn Road, Wisbech, at around 3.45am on April 4. She had been on a night out with her sister, but the pair had become separated at the filling station. Andrulionis was part of a group that had stopped at the same location. Earlier, he had tried to dance with the victim at a nearby pub but she rejected his advances. Andrulionis approached the victim and sat on a wall next to her, near the filling station, before dragging her into nearby bushes. The victim begged him not to rape her, but he placed his hands on her mouth and neck to stop her from screaming, leaving the victim fearing for her life. She tried to reason with him, but he continued with the attack, and she only managed to get away once he had raped her. Police were called and Andrulionis was arrested the following day. On Tuesday (September 15), at Cambridge Crown Court, Andrulionis, of Balding Close, Wisbech, was jailed. He pleaded guilty to one count of rape before the case went to trial. He was also ordered to spend six years on extended licence, handed an indefinite restraining order against the victim. Andrulionis was placed on the sex offenders register for life and must pay a victim surcharge of £228. Sentencing, Judge Andrew Hurst described him as “dangerous”, that he was only “faintly familiar” with the concept of consent and a “substantial risk” to other women. DC Michael Childs, who investigated, said: "Andrulionis is a predator who preyed on a victim in a vulnerable state and the lengthy sentence handed down reflects this. "I would like to pay tribute to the victim; her bravery in coming forward and supporting us with a prosecution is admirable and has led to a dangerous man being jailed for a long time." Visitors can enjoy a range of agricultural show attractions The programme includes livestock and equestrian competitions, produce displays, homecraft and flower-arranging classes. Visitors can also see vintage tractors, exhibitors and attractions across the showground. The show brings farmers, rural businesses, competitors, exhibitors and the public together to celebrate countryside life. The annual event celebrates rural life and the local community Visitors of all ages can learn about farming, rural skills and traditions. The showground will be open from 9am to 5.30pm, with free parking available. Children under 11 accompanied by an adult can enter free. Online tickets cost £18 for adults and £9 for children aged 11 to 16. Tickets bought on the day cost £20 for adults and £10 for children aged 11 to 16.
